newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First candidate urges tactical vote vs Prebble.
newsitem.headline: NZ First candidate urges tactical vote vs Prebble.

text.p: New Zealand First Wellington Central candidate Sarah Porter on Monday told her supporters to consider voting tactically to keep ACT New Zealand leader Richard Prebble out of parliament.
"Realistically, this constituency seat is a three-way race between National's Mark Thomas, Labour's Alick Shaw and ACT's Richard Prebble," Porter said in a statement.
She said she had observed the three candidates on the campaign trail and it was clear either Thomas or Shaw would be good representatives.
"Richard Prebble would be a disaster. The voters in Wellington Central are being used by him to advance ACT," Porter said.
"I'm calling on (United New Zealand candidate) Pauline Gardiner and the Alliance's Danna Glendining to put the interest of the electorate first and make the same statement."
Porter urged New Zealand First supporters to give New Zealand First their party list vote.
ACT is currently polling about four percent nationally but needs five percent support to be assured of seats in parliament after the October 12 election.
But if Prebble, who is running a close second in Wellington Central, wins the seat, ACT will be entitled to its share of seats without needing to breach the five percent threshold.
